evidence.location: section 0, RF-R5 and Standard move criteria SM2/SM3
evidence.observation: RF-R5 states "Re-exports do not carry patches across, so every `monkeypatch` of a moved name is pointed at the new location within the same move unit.", yet SM2 requires only that "For each `monkeypatch` of a moved name, a test patches the new location and observes the effect.", and RF-R6/SM3 widen only source-text scans (`inspect.getsource`, reads of `cli.py`, module-stays-unloaded checks). No criterion fails when an existing monkeypatch keeps targeting the old re-export path, where it patches a name no code reads and the guarding test passes vacuously.

concerns.recommendation: Add a standard move criterion plus a committed scan test in each move unit asserting that no test module patches a target listed in notes/shim-inventory.md, and that the RF0-counted files patching `gnd.cli` privates are repointed in the same unit; fold the scan's covered-set assertion into SM3.
concerns.title: Stale monkeypatch targets on old re-export paths are undetectable, so SM2 can pass while pins go vacuous

evidence.location: section 3 Sequence, versus section 0 RF-R1, predicate 1 and the r2 changes row F9
evidence.observation: Section 3 states "Every phase from RF2 on is behavior-preserving, with no exception (RF-R1)." and the r2 changes row for F9 reads "RF-R1 with no exceptions". RF-R1 itself retains an exception: "unless the owner rules a named exception that the phase spec states as its only observable change", and predicate 1 allows "a pin named by an owner-ruled exception under RF-R1". A phase gate reading section 3 cannot tell whether an owner-ruled observable change is admissible.

concerns.recommendation: Pick one rule and restate all three places consistently: either delete the owner-exception clause from RF-R1 and predicate 1, or qualify section 3 to say behavior-preserving except for an owner-ruled exception that the phase spec and record name as the only observable change.
concerns.title: Section 3's 'with no exception' contradicts the owner-exception clause retained in RF-R1 and predicate 1

evidence.location: predicate 5, section 4 RF0 tool paragraph, section 6 risk row 'Measurements mislead'
evidence.observation: Predicate 5 requires "a before/after table (SCCs, private cross-module imports, duplicate counts, largest-module sizes, co-change pairs)" and the risk row repeats "The close table reports private imports and co-change alongside SCCs.", but the RF0 tool is specified to report only "module-level and lazy edges, strongly connected components, imports of another module's private names, fan-in and fan-out, duplicate-helper candidates by name and body similarity, and the entry-point rule of RF5-C5". No committed artifact produces module sizes or co-change pairs, so the milestone cannot satisfy its own close predicate.

concerns.recommendation: Extend the RF0 tool specification (or name a second committed tool under `tools/`) to emit per-module line counts and a co-change pair ranking, and add an RF0 criterion that every column of the predicate 5 table is producible at the base commit and bound by digest in evidence/metrics-RF0.json.
concerns.title: Predicate 5's close table needs module sizes and co-change pairs that no phase commits to producing

evidence.location: section 0 RF-R9; section 4 RF5-C1 and RF6-C4; predicate 4
evidence.observation: RF-R9 requires "Every numeric target in a spec comes from the RF0 tool's measurement at that phase's base commit", but the line-based targets it must govern are RF5-C1 ("`cli.py` is at most 2,500 lines, and at most the lower ceiling the spec sets under RF-R9") and RF6-C4 ("the package split stays within its moved-line and touched-file budget"). The RF0 tool's output list contains no line count, module size or moved-line metric, and 2,500 is fixed in the plan rather than measured, so the derivation rule cannot be followed for these targets.

concerns.recommendation: Add line-count, module-size and moved-line metrics to the RF0 tool, or state in RF-R9 that size and moved-line budgets derive from a named measurement command recorded in the spec ledger; mark 2,500 explicitly as a plan ceiling a spec must lower rather than an RF-R9 target.
concerns.title: RF-R9 ties every numeric target to the RF0 tool, which reports no line, size or moved-line metric

evidence.location: predicate 3; section 4 RF0-C5 and RF2-C1; section 0 RF-R9
evidence.observation: Predicate 3 closes the milestone when "every family that the RF0 family list marks identical has exactly one definition" and RF2-C1 repeats it, but RF0-C5 only requires that "the pin-site inventory and the helper-family list are counted at execution time, not copied from the audit". No criterion requires each candidate the tool reports ("duplicate-helper candidates by name and body similarity") to be classified identical or diverged, so a list that marks few or none identical satisfies predicate 3 vacuously; RF-R9's anti-vacuity rule reaches only "Every numeric target in a spec".

concerns.recommendation: Add an RF0 criterion that every tool-reported duplicate candidate appears in notes/helper-families.md with a classification and reason, that the candidate/identical/diverged counts are recorded in evidence/metrics-RF0.json, and that RF2's scope is that whole identical set rather than a spec-selected subset.
concerns.title: Predicate 3 and RF2-C1 can pass vacuously because nothing forces the RF0 family list to classify every candidate

evidence.location: section 4 RF1 layering-test paragraph; SM4; RF3-C1
evidence.observation: RF1 adds "the layering test as a strict xfail (`strict=True`) scoped to the model, population, checking and semantics layers of the map", so the test is required to fail, yet SM4 says "the layering test still passes for every layer already declared clean" and RF3-C1 says "the layering test passes with its xfail marker removed" for "the core layers", a set the plan never maps onto those four named layers. Under strict=True an incidental cleanup (for example RF2 moving exit codes into `exits.py`) xpasses and turns a correct behavior-preserving move red with no stated rule for narrowing the marker.

concerns.recommendation: Require one xfail marker per layer or per wrong-way edge so a cleaned layer's marker is removed in the move unit that cleans it, define 'core layers' as the four named map layers, and restate SM4 as: no layer regresses from clean to failing, and no strict xfail xpasses without its marker being removed in the same unit.
concerns.title: Strict xfail makes SM4's 'still passes' undefined and can fail a correct move by xpass

evidence.location: section 4 RF0-C4; predicate 2; section 2 record-contract link
evidence.observation: RF0-C4 requires "the layer map covers every module, and a test fails on any module that has no entry", while predicate 2 scopes the same map to "every module under `src/gnd` (skills and examples excluded)". The plan's own record-contract link points at `src/gnd/skills/gnd-orm-core/references/milestone-record-format.md`, so packaged skills live under `src/gnd` and a coverage test written to RF0-C4's literal wording fails on every skills module.

concerns.recommendation: State the exclusion inside RF0-C4 (path-based rule or a declared list committed with the map) and require the coverage test to assert its excluded set explicitly, so RF0-C4 and predicate 2 describe the same scope.
concerns.title: RF0-C4's whole-repository map coverage contradicts predicate 2's skills and examples exclusion

evidence.location: section 0 RF-R4 and RF-R8; section 5 table row 'Packaged skills that cite module paths'
evidence.observation: RF-R4 defines a move unit as "one commit containing the move itself, its re-exports, its updates to `monkeypatch` targets and its widened source scans" and claims "Each move unit is green on its own against the phase's verification selection, so no commit leaves a patch or scan test red." But RF-R8 says "`production_identity` hashes every `src/gnd/**/*.py` file by path, and the distribution-lane manifest pins the source bytes", and section 5 says packaged-skill pin sites are "updated in the move unit that moves the module". Neither the manifest/identity update nor the skill citation updates appear in RF-R4's enumerated contents.

concerns.recommendation: Enumerate the distribution manifest and production_identity regeneration plus packaged-skill citation updates in RF-R4 (subject to RF-R7's sign-off limit), or state which tests are excluded from a move unit's green requirement while RF-D3 is unresolved and how that intermediate red state is recorded.
concerns.title: RF-R4's atomic move unit omits the manifest, identity and skill-citation updates other rules require in it

evidence.observation: Predicate 2 fails only on a wrong-way import "that is not on its allow-list", where an entry needs only "a reason and the successor work that would remove it", and RF4-C4 permits "Any remaining wrong-way edge is on the allow-list of predicate 2, and the spec names it." No count, bound or shrink requirement applies to the allow-list, and RF-R9 budgets only "Every numeric target in a spec", so a phase could allow-list every wrong-way edge and still satisfy predicate 2 and RF4-C4.

concerns.recommendation: Bring the allow-list under RF-R9: count its entries at RF0, record the count per phase in evidence/metrics-<phase>.json, and require it to be non-increasing and strictly lower in any phase whose criteria claim layering progress.
concerns.title: The layering allow-list has no budget or shrink rule, so predicate 2 can pass with layering unchanged

evidence.location: section 0 RF-R7; r2 changes row 'Divergent: source-side edits undetectable'
evidence.observation: RF-R7 makes the stronger control conditional: "If the source is reachable, the gate also records a high-water-mark comparison; otherwise the record says the control rests on attestation." Reachability is undefined and judged by the same owner who attests, so the high-water-mark comparison can be skipped at every gate and the r2 repair for the r1 view 'source-side edits undetectable' reduces to attestation in practice.

concerns.recommendation: Define reachability as a recorded attempt (the command run and the commit it resolved to, or the failure output), require the high-water-mark comparison whenever the attempt succeeds, and require the failure reason in the phase record when it does not.
concerns.title: RF-R7's 'if the source is reachable' is a self-judged escape hatch around the high-water-mark control

evidence.location: section 10 RF-D2; section 3 Sequence; section 6 risk row 'The milestone drifts'
evidence.observation: RF-D2 states "Recording that is a public-launch act: this plan cannot bind public-launch, so RF2 waits for it" and section 3 confirms "RF2 and every later phase wait for the conditions in RF-D2." The only drift control is "If two consecutive phases miss an RF-R9 target, the owner re-plans before the next phase begins", which cannot fire while no phase has started, so a delayed public-launch Phase 4 sign-off parks the milestone indefinitely with no recorded route.

concerns.recommendation: Record a stall condition for the RF-D2 dependency (for example: if RF2 has not started by the next owner gate or a stated window, the owner either re-plans around RF0/RF1-only scope or rules a revised sequence) and add it as a row in the section 6 risk table.
concerns.title: The RF-D2 wait on public-launch sign-off has no stall or fallback condition

evidence.location: section 4 RF4 body and RF4-C4; RF5 'Parts'; RF6 'Parts'; section 6 risk row 'Phases grow into rewrites'
evidence.observation: RF4 bundles five restructurings (safefs visibility, splitting `agent_cli` into `process.py` and `agents.py`, re-routing `diff`, making the synth oracle public as `synth/oracle/`, and reordering assurance into `gnd/assurance/`) and carries the widest criterion in the plan, RF4-C4: "the layering test's scope covers every layer of the map, and the test passes." The rewrite control names only "RF-R9 budgets, the RF5 limit of three parts, the RF6a/RF6b split"; RF4 has no parts mechanism.

concerns.recommendation: Give RF4 an explicit numbered parts split with its own spec gate and record (for example safefs/agent_cli/diff, then the synth oracle, then the assurance package), or state in the RF4 spec why one unit stays inside its RF-R9 touched-file and moved-line budget while also clearing whole-map layering.
concerns.title: RF4 carries whole-map layering criteria and five restructurings but no parts limit, unlike RF5 and RF6

evidence.location: section 4 RF8 body; section 10 RF-D8; Inspection baseline paragraph; section 4 RF3 body
evidence.observation: RF8 instructs "Name the version-8 literal and remove the dead first assignment of `SESSION_CONTRACT_VERSION`. Both are non-observable (RF-D8)." The baseline convention covers only numbers: "**Every other number in this plan is an audit claim that has not been re-proved.** Where such a number appears it is marked *(audit)*", so the load-bearing claims that the assignment is dead and that both edits are non-observable carry no marker and no confirmation criterion; RF3's named `checker.py` rebindings are likewise taken from the audit unmarked.

concerns.recommendation: Mark these as unverified audit claims and add an obligation (RF0 or the RF8 spec) to confirm deadness and non-observability at the phase base commit before the edit, recording the confirmation and the pin evidence in the phase record.
concerns.title: RF8 acts on the audit's 'dead assignment' and 'non-observable' claims without the plan's own marking or a confirmation step

evidence.location: RF3-C1; section 4 RF6 body; section 0 RF-R9
evidence.observation: RF3-C1 requires "the core layers contain no multi-module SCC, lazy edges counted, and the layering test passes with its xfail marker removed", while RF6 defers the structural work on the two largest core files: "Only then split `model.py` and `checker.py` into packages along their existing sections." If a cycle RF0-C2 confirms runs through edges only that split can sever, RF3-C1 is unreachable and the sole route is RF-R9's generic "A target that proves unreachable stops the phase and returns it to the owner gate with the measured value."

concerns.recommendation: Add an explicit route in RF3: either permit the specific split needed to sever a confirmed edge to be pulled forward into RF3 as a recorded scope change, or permit a bounded allow-list entry whose removal is a named obligation of RF6b.
concerns.title: RF3-C1 demands the core SCC be gone before the model/checker split that RF6b owns, with no fallback

evidence.observation: RF1-C1 requires "every pin fails against a seeded mutation of the code it pins", but no harness, mutation list or result artifact is named: section 2 provides only "`evidence/metrics-<phase>.json`: tool output at the phase's base and head commits, bound by digest", and RF1-C2 confines the diff to "only test, fixture and tool files". The criterion can be asserted from unrecorded manual edits, leaving the central pin-strength claim unauditable.

concerns.recommendation: Name the mutation mechanism (a committed tool under `tools/` or a mutation table recorded in the RF1 spec), require at least one seeded mutation per pinned surface, and bind the pass/fail results in evidence/metrics-RF1.json.
concerns.title: RF1-C1's seeded-mutation criterion has no named harness or evidence home

evidence.observation: Predicate 4 is titled "**Thin entry points:**" and enforces "`cli.py` is at most 2,500 lines" plus an entry-point rule whose scope is "each `commands/<group>.py` module imports domain behavior only from `gnd.api`, a lane `service` module, `gnd.exits`, `commands/_output` or the named allow-list". Since RF5 also says "`cli.py` stays as a file", nothing constrains what the surviving `cli.py` imports, so 2,500 lines of direct domain imports inside `cli.py` satisfies predicate 4 and RF5-C2 while the thin-entry-point claim fails.

concerns.recommendation: Extend the entry-point rule to `cli.py` itself under the same allow-list, or require the RF5 record to enumerate every remaining domain import in `cli.py` with a reason and a successor obligation.
concerns.title: Predicate 4 binds only commands modules, leaving the surviving cli.py imports unconstrained

evidence.location: predicate 4; section 4 RF0 body; section 4 RF5 criteria list
evidence.observation: Predicate 4 cites "The RF0 tool's entry-point rule (RF5-C5)" and the RF0 body commits the tool to report "the entry-point rule of RF5-C5", but the RF5 criteria list defines only RF5-C1 and RF5-C2, with the rule text in RF5-C2. A milestone-close predicate points at an identifier that does not exist in the plan.

concerns.recommendation: Repoint predicate 4 and the RF0 body to RF5-C2, or introduce a stable named rule identifier that the tool specification, RF0 and RF5-C2 all cite.
concerns.title: Predicate 4 and the RF0 body cite RF5-C5, which the plan never defines

evidence.location: Status paragraph; r2 changes table, rows beginning 'Divergent:'; section 8
evidence.observation: The status paragraph claims "r2 repairs every agreed concern group and five of the six divergent views (see *r2 changes* at the end)", but the r2 changes table lists six rows beginning "Divergent:" (RF-D2 ends before publication; thin session replay; source-side edits undetectable; non-strict xfail; diverged families not enumerated; RF6 split uncovered). The divergent view left unrepaired is not identified, so section 8's route ("residual concerns go to the RF0 spec gate as recorded open questions") has no named residual to carry.

concerns.recommendation: Either correct the count to six or name the divergent view r2 did not repair, with the reason, and record it as an open question for the RF0 spec gate.
concerns.title: Status claims five of six divergent views repaired while the r2 table lists six repairs, leaving the residual untracked

summary: r2 repairs the r1 concern groups in substance: audit numbers are demoted to marked claims with criteria restated over the RF0 inventory, a layer map and RF0-C4 arrive, RF-R9 adds anti-vacuity and stop conditions, RF-R4/SM2/SM3 make move units atomic, the xfail is strict, and section 10 splits ruled from open. Most phase criteria are falsifiable. Three issues still block a clean demonstration: nothing detects a monkeypatch left pointing at an old re-export, so SM2 can pass while the pins go vacuous; section 3's 'with no exception' contradicts the owner-exception clause retained in RF-R1 and predicate 1; and predicate 5's close table requires largest-module sizes and co-change pairs that the RF0 tool's stated outputs do not produce. The rest are hardening gaps in budget derivation, allow-list bounds, xfail semantics, map-coverage wording, move-unit contents and the RF-D2 stall route, plus two internal-reference inconsistencies.
